rules.title: Just cause requirement for termination of tenancy (Civil Code 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause (at-fault or no-fault, as listed in the section), and the just cause must be stated in the written notice to terminate. If adult tenants are added before an existing tenant has occupied for 24 months, the rule applies only if all tenants have occupied for 12 months or more or one or more tenants have occupied for 24 months or more.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of continuous and lawful occupancy (or 24 months for at least one tenant when adult tenants are added)
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property where a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months, unless an exemption in subdivision (e) applies or the property is governed by a qualifying local just cause ordinance.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly or adult residential facilities; dormitories owned and operated by higher education institutions or K-12 schools; housing where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with an owner who lives there; single-family owner-occupied residences where the owner rents no more than two units or bedrooms, and mobilehomes; owner-occupied two-unit properties in a single structure (neither an ADU/JADU); housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management, where the tenants received the required written exemption notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income households.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply renders the written termination notice void. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, reasonable attorney's fees and costs in the court's discretion, and up to three times actual damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct, plus possible punitive damages; the Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault just cause terminations
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination of a tenancy covered by the just cause rule, the owner must, regardless of tenant income, either make a direct relocation payment or waive in writing the final month's rent, equal to one month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice was issued. Relocation assistance must be provided within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, and the termination notice must inform the tenant of this right.
rules.key_value: One month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice to terminate was issued
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies for which just cause is required under subdivision (a) that are terminated for a no-fault just cause.

rules.exemptions: A tenant found by a government agency or court to be at fault for the condition triggering an order to vacate is not entitled to relocation assistance.
rules.penalty: An owner's failure to strictly comply renders the notice of termination void. If the tenant fails to vacate after the notice expires, the relocation assistance or rent waiver is recoverable as damages in an action to recover possession.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: The relocation assistance or rent waiver required by this subdivision shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.

rules.title: Opportunity to cure before termination for curable lease violation
rules.requirement: Before issuing a notice to terminate for a curable lease violation, the owner must first give notice of the violation with an opportunity to cure; only if the violation is not cured within the stated time may a three-day notice to quit without an opportunity to cure be served.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property subject to the just cause requirement terminating for a curable lease violation.
rules.quoted_span: If the violation is not cured within the time period set forth in the notice, a three-day notice to quit without an opportunity to cure may thereafter be served to terminate the tenancy.

rules.title: Required notice to tenants of rent cap and just cause protections
rules.requirement: Owners of property subject to the section must give tenants a notice, in no less than 12-point type, stating that California law limits rent increases and requires a statement of cause to terminate a tenancy, in the lease, an addendum or a signed written notice; for tenancies existing before July 1, 2020, by written notice no later than August 1, 2020, or as an addendum.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property subject to Civil Code Section 1946.2.
